record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: Let f be a Lebesgue-measure-preserving smooth diffeomorphism of the closed disk D² with only finitely many periodic points. Must f be C^∞-conjugate to the rigid rotation r_α(z) = exp(2πiα) z for a suitable angle α?

evidence.quote: When f is Lebesgue measure preserving and f has a finite number of periodic points is f C∞-conjugated to rα ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}^2 = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1\}$ denote the closed unit disk, equipped with Lebesgue (area) measure. Let $f : \mathbb{D}^2 \to \mathbb{D}^2$ be a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism that preserves Lebesgue measure and has only finitely many periodic points (counting all periods). For $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, let $r_\alpha : \mathbb{D}^2 \to \mathbb{D}^2$ denote the rigid rotation $r_\alpha(z) = e^{2\pi i \alpha} z$.

Question: Must there exist $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ and a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $h : \mathbb{D}^2 \to \mathbb{D}^2$ such that $h \circ f \circ h^{-1} = r_\alpha$?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal active related research on area-preserving disk diffeomorphisms, mixing constructions, and conjugacy of circle maps to rigid rotations, but no source asserts a resolution of the specific rigidity question on the closed disk under the finite-periodic-points hypothesis. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On mixing diffeomorphisms of the disk
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of smooth area-preserving diffeomorphisms of the disk with prescribed dynamics; no claim of resolving the finite-periodic-points conjugacy question.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on area-preserving disk diffeomorphisms does not resolve the conjugacy rigidity question.

status_evidence.title: Periodic points of Hamiltonian surface diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Studies periodic point structure for area-preserving surface diffeomorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Surface periodic point theory is active but does not settle this disk rigidity problem.
